bugs.title: A clean player revealed during an ad pod plays several seconds behind live and never closes the gap
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: The clean player was only pulled onto the live edge when it was MORE than 20s behind AND only while an ad was active. A warm standby minted at page load sits wherever hls.js joined the live window (5-19s behind), so it passed the gate unchanged and was revealed one segment-delay behind the native. hls.js then plays at 1x and can never close a constant offset, so the delay was permanent for the whole pod. The user's own observation that dragging the bar forward a few seconds keeps working proves a forward seek inside the live window is safe, so the extension had no reason to leave the offset there. The same 20s gate also gated `healthy`, so a 12s-behind standby was considered fit to show.
bugs.falsifier: With a standby 12s behind the live edge, a reveal must hand the user a picture at the same offset as the native (within 3s of the edge). If the revealed player is left 12s behind, or is revealed without a seek, the fix did not take.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'quando troca o player porque ele protege de um ad, a live volta varios segundos'

Pre-fix code, kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js: frame-stats handler `if (overlay.adActive && typeof m.st.lat === 'number' && m.st.lat > 20) { ... seek to pos+lat-3 }` and `const latOk = ... || m.st.lat <= 20`. standby-start had its own 20s gate (`lat0 > 20`) and revealed without any catch-up below that

Fix (0.8.44): CLEAN_LAT_TARGET=3 / CLEAN_LAT_MAX=8 / RESUME_GAP_SEC=1.5, a single catchUpClean(st, force) helper shared by the frame-stats tick and by reveal, called for `overlay.adActive || overlay.standby`, plus a forced re-align at reveal when the standby is more than target+1.5s behind. cleanLatTarget() aims the clean player at the NATIVE's own offset captured at take-over (min 8, max 2 clamp) so the swap lands on the wall-clock second the user was watching

Negative arm: restoring the pre-fix gate (`(overlay.adActive || overlay.standby)` -> `overlay.adActive && lat > 20`) makes the detector FAIL with the player left 12s behind, so the check measures the fix and not the harness

bugs.title: Ad-end jumps the picture: the native was seeked to its buffered end and resumed 300ms late through a lifecycle gate
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: resumeNative() seeked the native to `buffered.end - 0.5`, which is the newest frame the ELEMENT holds, not the offset the clean player was showing. On a native Twitch paused while it was covered that is a seek across the whole pod (a visible jump); on one that kept buffering it is a free jump forward past the clean position. Independently, ad-end called resumeNativeIfAllowed(), which refuses while `overlay.adActive` is still set and a revealed frame is still mounted - both true at that moment - so the hand-back was deferred to the 300ms retry, i.e. a frozen native frame followed by a jump.
bugs.falsifier: At ad-end the native must already stand at the offset the clean player had (edge - cleanLatTarget, within 1.5s), with no seek at all when it is already there. A hand-back that moves the native by seconds, or that leaves it frozen for a retry, is the defect.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'quando acaba o ad e o player volta, aí acontece um salto no tempo por causa disso'

Pre-fix code: `const be = v.buffered && v.buffered.length ? v.buffered.end(v.buffered.length - 1) : 0; if (be > v.currentTime + 3) { v.currentTime = be - 0.5 }` and ad-end `resumeNativeIfAllowed(v, 'now')` where that helper returns early on `overlay.adActive` / revealed frame

Fix (0.8.44): the hand-off seeks to `nativeEdge - cleanLatTarget()` (skip when the gap is under RESUME_GAP_SEC, log from/to/lat/gap), and ad-end resumes the native DIRECTLY under the user-intent guard only, so the frame and the picture change in the same tick

kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs drives the REAL kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js through the shared stubbed DOM (mute-decision-test.cjs makePage/settle) and through the real ad path (ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal -> ad-end): `ad-end on a native already at the target offset does not seek` and `a native parked behind by the pod is handed back at edge-3`
Negative arm: restoring the buffered-end target makes the detector FAIL with ct=399.5 against a 397 target (a 2.5s jump), so the check is exercised
node kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs -> RESULT PASS checks=13 failed=0

bugs.title: A mute change made during the swap is inverted: the extension reads its own write as the user's decision
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: The user's mute decision was captured ONCE at take-over (adoptNativeMute/overlay.muteIntent) and never tracked afterwards, so an unmute during the pod reached the clean player only if the generic pointerdown handler fired - and that handler returned early for `overlay.muteIntent`, i.e. exactly the case of a user who had muted. The reverse direction came from the autoplay muting: the extension muted the clean frame to get it to play, and nothing marked that mute as OURS, so `autoplayMuted` was never set and the reveal treated the silence as the user's, while a page click later unmuted a user who had asked for silence.
bugs.falsifier: Unmute while the clean player covers the ad: the clean player must become audible immediately, and the ad-end hand-back must NOT re-mute the native. Mute, then click anywhere in the page: it must stay silent.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'eu desmutar rapidamente a live quando acontece o ad e troca de player, faz ele mutar o player. ou vice versa'

Pre-fix code: `document` pointerdown handler `if (!explicit && overlay.muteIntent) return;` (a muted user could never be unmuted by the flow that was supposed to unlock them) and reveal paths sending `mute: true` for autoplay with no flag distinguishing an autoplay mute from a user mute

Fix (0.8.44): a capture-phase `volumechange` listener (onNativeVolumeChange) tracks the user's decision continuously while the ad path owns playback, ignores our own writes within 400ms via noteMuteWrite(), forwards the decision to the revealed clean player immediately, and clears autoplayMuted on an explicit unmute. The pointerdown unlock now requires `overlay.autoplayMuted` before it may overrule silence

bugs.title: The stream keeps the previous channel after an SPA channel switch (revealed clean player is never stopped)
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: Twitch changes channels with an SPA navigation: same document, same content-script instance, new location.pathname. The ad-free clean player is an overlay owned by that instance. The only channel checks in twitch-adblock.js were inside ad-hold/standby-start and they only applied while the overlay was an invisible STANDBY (`if (!overlay.standby) return` / `overlay.standby ? stop : cold path`). An overlay that was already revealed (a live ad pod) had no channel check and nothing in the module watched the route (no popstate/pushState/pathname poll), so after a switch the previous channel clean player stayed on screen, the native player stayed visibility:hidden/muted, and the next ad on the new channel also hit the early `overlay.frame && !overlay.standby` return. The user sees the previous streamer image and calls it "keeps the last stream".
bugs.falsifier: With a revealed clean player on channel A, changing location.pathname to channel B (the way Twitch does, no reload) must remove the A player and hand the native B player back instead of keeping the A stream attached.

Pre-fix code, same module: no route watcher at all (grep popstate|pushState|setInterval|pathname found only pageChannel() and the document_start standby requests)

bugs.hypothesis: The mute/volume intent was one shared row (`ko.v2.vols`) written by whichever tab the user touched and fed back into EVERY tab by `chrome.storage.onChanged` -> `applyVols(s.vols)` -> `KOAudio.setIntent(...)` -> `apply()`. Since ko-audio derives `muted = intent || policy || surface !== visible`, a mute in tab A silenced tab B's native player within one storage round-trip, and the same path carried an unmute the other way ('e vice versa'). A reload of one tab, or any saveState from it, also clobbered the stored row for everyone.
bugs.falsifier: Two tabs sharing the `ko.v2` record: a gesture in A must not change B's arbiter intent. tab-audio-scope-test.cjs fabricates two worlds from the real ko-audio.js; the pre-fix shape is the positive control (feeding a shared row into a tab DOES mute it) and two source mutations re-insert the shared row and the listener write, both caught by the fence.
evidence: kick-overlay/tab-audio-scope-test.cjs — checks=11 failed=0 (A's gesture invisible to B, reload restores only its own choice, fresh tab at defaults, mirror reads the arbiter, positive control, 2 fence mutations)
_tools/ko-verify.mjs RESULT PASS checks=20 failed=0 (tab-audio-scope wired into the gate)

LIVE guest Chrome 0.8.53, twitch.tv/kaicenat (native player, two real tabs), `node _tools/ko-harness.mjs tabmute`: before A={intent false, vol 0.5, native false} B={false,0.5}; mute in A -> A={true,0} B unchanged {false,0.5}; unmute A -> A false; mute in B -> B={true,0} A unchanged {false,0.5}; unmute B -> false. bugs.title: A hand-back seeked a native whose timeline had already reset, producing a longer delay than before the pod
bugs.hypothesis: The wall-clock recovery assumed the native's timeline is the one it held at take-over. Measured in the guest Chrome on a live Twitch element: pausing the <video> for 22 s EMPTIES it and it reloads from 0, i.e. AT the live edge (`ct 211.8 buf 212.9` -> `ct 0 buf null rs 1`). `holdCt` then names a timeline that no longer exists, so `behind = elapsed - advanced` measured the reload plus the pod and the recovery seeked forward by tens of seconds. His own ko.adlog 2026-11-13 shows the target that arithmetic produced (`to:172` on a 42.4 s window).
bugs.falsifier: With a native 211.8 s into the pod and the element reloaded to 0 before the hand-back, `native-timeline-reset` must be logged once naming `holdCt 211.8`, and the element must receive ZERO writes to `currentTime`. evidence: Guest measurement 2026-11-15 on a live Twitch element (twitch.tv/rodil): pausing for 22 s empties the element and it reloads at 0, i.e. the live edge; the sentinel edge (1073741824) means the wall clock was the only timeline the old code had

Fix: `twitch-adblock.js` compares the native's `currentTime` at hand-back with the position captured at take-over; an element that went BACKWARDS by more than RESUME_GAP_SEC did not freeze, it reloaded, and is reported via `native-timeline-reset {holdCt, ct, elapsed}` with no seek

bugs.title: A catch-up seek landed with one second of buffer left, because a frontier-gap branch overrode the runway the health gate demands
bugs.hypothesis: The catch-up ceiling was `pos + hold - 1`, so a seek could land with a single second of media in hand, and the guard `runway >= HEALTH_BUFFER_SEC || frontierGap >= 2` let a large frontier gap override exactly that starvation. The ceiling existed to prevent 2026-11-08's four-for-four `overlay-stall-stop`; the disjunct re-opened the same door for the case that actually fires.
bugs.falsifier: With a standby at `pos:160, hold:6, lat:18.8`, every catch-up seek must move the playhead at most `pos + hold - HEALTH_BUFFER_SEC = +3 s`. If any seek moves further, the landing starves the buffer.
evidence: Owner's own 0.8.91 ko.adlog 2026-11-15: `overlay-catchup {hold:6, lat:18.8, pos:160, source:"standby"}` — a 1 s landing with a 12.8 s frontier gap

Fix: `ceiling = pos + hold - HEALTH_BUFFER_SEC`, and the `|| frontierGap >= 2` disjunct deleted (with the ceiling in place it could only ever admit a starving seek); the dead `runway` re-check was removed with it rather than left as a check that cannot fail
Arm `ad-time-continuity`: 'a catch-up lands with the health gate\'s runway, not on the buffer frontier' (`moved <= 3.05` and `>= 1.5`)
RED arm: restoring `ceiling = pos + hold - 1` moves 5.00 s into a 6 s buffer

bugs.title: A dead overlay layer kept publishing data-ko-owner="kick", so the ad path believed the native was covered
